Adding nodes

The panel is the control plane; each OVNode is a VPN server. Nodes never call the panel — the panel connects out to them, so the panel is the only thing you register.

Pick a topology

  • One box — panel and node on the same VPS. The easiest option, and plenty for personal use and small teams. The panel's Ready card prints a ready-to-paste command with the API key already filled in.
  • Panel here, VPN servers there — install a node on each VPN server and register them all in the one panel. Adding a node never changes the panel install.

Because the direction of travel is always panel → node, you can move or replace the panel at any time without touching the VPN servers.

1. Install the node agent

On the VPN server (not the panel server, unless you are doing the all-in-one setup):

OVNode is a separate project: github.com/anonysec/OVNode.

The installer asks one question — but you can be asked nothing: pick the recommended 1. Install for a default host service. For every setting, run interactive for the full wizard:

The node installer is driven by variables and -y. The panel's same-server offer asks for the VPN port and protocol first; the standalone install takes them from the environment:

The flags are -y/--yes and -h/--help; everything else is a PascalCase variable. There is no Docker mode. The relevant variables are:

VariableDefaultMeaning
InstanceovnodeInstance name; selects /opt/<name>, /var/lib/<name> and <name>.service
NodeNameovnodeNode name — must match the panel exactly
ApiKeygeneratedAPI key, minimum 16 characters
ApiPort2083Sync API port the panel connects to
VpnPorts1194VPN ports; every port gets a connection block in each profile
Protoudpudp, tcp or both
TlsMethodselfsignedselfsigned, letsencrypt, letsencrypt-ip or custom
TlsDomain—Domain, for the Let's Encrypt modes
Ipv6off1 adds a ULA pool and an IPv6 route push
NoNatoff1 skips forwarding, NAT and port redirects
Repoanonysec/OVNodePull releases from a fork

Install the agent once per VPN server. Save the API key it prints; the panel needs it next. The installer also prints the node summary (name, service URL, API key) for the next step.

Protocol. Proto=both runs one OpenVPN process per transport on the same port, and every profile carries a connection block for each. That is the recommended setup for networks that filter UDP or TCP (see the OVNode ISP compatibility page). Everything else tunable — port, extra ports, max clients, keepalive, DNS, routes, IPv6, MTU/mssfix, ciphers, TLS floor — is changed from the panel's node drawer, not by editing files.

2. Register it in the panel

Go to Nodes → Add Node and paste the bundle from the node's ready card into the form, or type the fields. Turn TLS on (the node always serves HTTPS — plain HTTP is not offered, because the API key travels in a header on every request) and save.

A green row means the panel reached the node. Tests run from the panel; if the row is red, check the sync API port, the API key and the node's firewall.

All-in-one: panel and node on one box

Same two steps. Install the node on the panel server, then in Nodes → Add Node use:

  • Address: 127.0.0.1 — same machine, no firewall work needed
  • Name: exactly the OVN_NAME you passed to the node installer
  • Port: 2083, API key: the key from the node install
  • TLS: whatever the node uses

Ports

PortWhatReachable from
2095 (or yours)Panel web UIOnly you — your browser
2083Node sync APIOnly the panel's IP
1194 (plus any extra VPN ports)OpenVPN clientsEveryone

The node installer opens the firewall for you. If your provider has its own firewall (security groups, cloud firewalls), open them yourself: 1194 on UDP and TCP, plus any additional VPN ports you configured. Open 2083 only from the panel.

If the summary shows a private address (10.x, 192.168.x) the server is behind NAT — put its public IP in the panel instead. Open the VPN ports yourself on both UDP and TCP, and the sync API port only from the panel.

Node data, backup and reinstall

A node has no database. Its state is plain files: 

/var/lib/ovnode/openvpn/server/   server.conf, PKI (CA, certificates, CRL), logs
/var/lib/ovnode/openvpn/server/users/   users/<cn>/{name,state,client.ovpn}, sessions/, usage/, scripts/
/var/lib/ovnode/   agent data (flat, one instance = one directory)
/var/backups/      backup archives (root-only)

ovnode backup archives /var/lib/ovnode and the OpenVPN PKI into root-only tarballs in /var/backups, keeping the newest 14 unless you pass --keep N. ovnode restore takes a safety copy before it replaces anything and refuses to continue if it cannot. ovnode uninstall keeps the data; ovnode uninstall --purge deletes it.

The panel database is the panel side of disaster recovery. See Backups & restore.
